    Self-evolving training improves the performance of agents on difficult tasks through verifiable feedback, but it often applies costly deliberation uniformly across tasks. To address this problem, we propose Mode-Optimized Reasoning with Self-Adaptive Effort (MORE), a self-evolving training framework that adaptively selects both reasoning form and computational effort for each task. Specifically, MORE follows a two-stage training paradigm: (i) \emph{Stage 1} establishes a compact prior over direct answering, short and long chain-of-thought, and code-based reasoning, and (ii) \emph{Stage 2} self-evolves this prior with Mode-Adaptive and Test-time Effort PPO (MATE-PPO) on generated, verifiable task streams without curated data. By learning mode selection and token expenditure jointly, MORE allocates concise reasoning to tasks that permit it while retaining extended deliberation where it is useful. Across coding, mathematics, and general-reasoning benchmarks, MORE achieves consistent performance gains on Base and Coder backbones at model scales from 3B to 14B.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Many mathematical research agents focus on solving problems with fixed statements. However, conjecture research, especially in applied mathematics, may require revising candidate questions or conclusions as investigation proceeds, coupling problem formulation with proof development. We present PACE, a research-proof agent that supports this process through a structured research loop that selects mathematical objectives and develops or challenges candidate mechanisms. The whole prover constructs proofs from these mechanisms, and an independent verifier checks them against the original target. Evidence-tracking memory stores assumptions and dependencies arising during research and marks evidence for revalidation when a candidate or condition changes. This memory supports task-specific context composition that keeps checked premises, exploratory material and unresolved obligations distinct. To evaluate proof construction and conjecture research, we introduce ResearchProofBench, an applied-mathematics benchmark focused on optimization, comprising 51 known-proof tasks with 331 hidden checkpoints under historical abstract access and six open-problem cases. The known-proof tasks assess reconstruction of published results, while the open-problem cases assess mathematical investigation and proof development. On the 51 known-proof tasks, PACE achieves an aggregate Proof Score of 75.16 and completes 20 proofs. In conjecture research, PACE develops conditional results, with its submissions receiving higher review scores than the compared baselines.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper investigates why vision-language models fail to combine correctly recovered facts into valid decisions, using probes and activation replacement to examine solution-related internal information.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Multimodal reasoning requires models to combine multiple pieces of evidence into decisions that satisfy all relevant constraints. Evaluations centered on final-answer accuracy leave unclear whether failures arise from reading individual facts or using them together. We study this question through the multi-evidence integration gap, linking local fact recovery to global decision validity on controlled subset-selection and path-finding tasks. Our evaluation combines conditional performance given correct local answers with same-grid local queries, text-oracle inputs, retrieval controls, and constraint ablations. We further examine hidden-state probes and activation replacement across network depth, token positions, and model families. Across the evaluated models, accurate local recovery coexists with substantial global failure. For example, Gemma-3-27B recovers all evaluated isolated item facts correctly but achieves only 19.75% global validity on eight-item visual instances. Probes decode information about solution membership from global-prompt states, while corresponding clean-state replacement recovers failed decisions over model-dependent depth ranges. These findings show that recovering facts and representing solution-related information are insufficient for reliable joint decisions. They motivate evaluations and model improvements that explicitly target how available evidence is combined, alongside advances in perception and model scale.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) trains a student on its own reasoning trajectories using token-level supervision from a reference-conditioned teacher initialized from the same model. However, access to the reference can induce teacher behaviors that undermine independent reasoning in thinking models, leading to reference hallucinations, where the student cites an unavailable reference to justify reasoning steps, and reconsideration suppression, where the teacher discourages verification and revision at uncertain steps. We introduce Steered-Teacher OPSD (ST-OPSD) to jointly address these failure modes through activation steering. ST-OPSD extracts two directions from model-generated reasoning trajectories and applies them to the teacher's hidden states during distillation target computation, suppressing reference-invoking behavior and encouraging reconsideration with marker-family calibration. The student learns from the resulting teacher distributions without being steered. Experiments on AIME and HMMT show that ST-OPSD improves accuracy over vanilla OPSD and other interventions while restoring reconsideration and reference-hallucination rates to base-model levels.

    Large language models (LLMs) generally lack deep causal reasoning capabilities in temporal reasoning. Inspired by document layout reordering, this paper proposes a paradigm shift from discrete narratives to causal topologies. It constructs two architectures: a training-free neuro-symbolic framework, temporal causal reasoning agent (TCR-Agent), which achieves interpretable causal deduction and counterfactual truncation through external causal graph instantiation and a symbolic intervention engine; and an end-to-end model, temporal causal reasoning former (TCR-Former), which internalizes these mechanisms into the Transformer attention space via a Causal-Topological Attention Mask and temporal span biases. At the same time, TCR-Former achieves an accuracy 16.5% higher than that of state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, outperforming large-scale models such as GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek-V3.2 with only approximately 8.6B parameters. Further analysis reveals a structure-reasoning disconnection phenomenon in existing methods: external symbolic constraints and chain-of-thought reasoning can improve reasoning steps, yet fail to enhance deep causal deductive capability. By internalizing temporal causal reasoning capabilities into the model, TCR-Former effectively bridges this gap, providing an efficient and reliable end-to-end foundation for complex reasoning scenarios.

    ENGLISH

    Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) enables large language models (LLMs) to continuously self-improve their reasoning capabilities. Compared to RLVR's scalar rewards, recent self-supervised on-policy distillation methods leverage denser supervision signals. However, both paradigms suffer from exploration bottlenecks, struggling to escape local optima when the policy fails to sample valid solutions. Relying on external demonstrations can bypass this issue; however, the off-policy nature hinders genuine self-improvement and the mismatched-distribution reasoning can not be fully exploited. In this work, we propose Self-Evolution Policy Optimization (SEPO), a framework that drives continuous reasoning capability evolution via guided exploration and in-distribution exploitation. Specifically, SEPO utilizes labels to elicit correct reasoning from the policy, unlocking the exploration potential. By treating current policy conditioned on this in-distribution reasoning as a self-teacher, SEPO distills the newly discovered solution back into the policy. Through this iterative cycle of policy-intrinsic exploration and exploitation, SEPO achieves robust and continuous capability evolution. Across scientific, tool-use, and complex logical reasoning domains, SEPO consistently achieves the best performance under identical training time or steps, demonstrating superior efficiency and convergence ceilings. Notably, SEPO maintains stable improvements even in scenarios where baselines severely underperform or fail entirely, such as on complex tasks or with small-scale models. Our code is available at https://github.com/Eric8932/SEPO.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    In this paper, we introduce $\Delta\tau$-Bench, an executable agent benchmark that models the structural evolution of large tool ecosystems. In $\Delta\tau$-Bench, independently evolving services continually reshape how tasks can be accomplished: familiar tools may disappear or be replaced, while more efficient alternatives emerge amid overlapping functionality and noisy documentation. Against this moving capability frontier, we evaluate whether agents can proactively discover efficient tool-use paths and promptly revise their accumulated procedural knowledge, bringing together demands that existing benchmarks fail to examine. $\Delta\tau$-Bench comprises 1,588 validated multi-turn tasks across 42 domains and six successive ecosystem states generated through capability-preserving transformations. Our evaluation shows that even the strongest evaluated model or harness achieves only 42.3% task success, while initial gains from existing skill-learning methods can not consistently translate into better adaptation as the ecosystem evolves. These findings motivate Steward, an ecosystem manager that jointly manages tools and procedural knowledge through incremental skill maintenance and dynamic provisioning during task execution. Experiments show that Steward sustains higher task success across ecosystem changes with lower skill-maintenance overhead, while improving both recovery from disrupted workflows and adoption of more efficient alternatives.

    Matched Capabilities, Different Behaviors: A Controlled Study of MCP and CLI Interfaces for Language Agents

    Zhenning Shi, Liang Pang, Yongqi Li

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The study shows that tool-interface representations alter agents’ action choices, failures, recovery, and subsequent trajectories, then introduces a repair method that improves performance and cost. This is a core Systems contribution on agent interfaces and interaction; its decision-behavior analysis has a partial connection to Reasoning, but does not investigate internal model mechanisms or compositional generalization.

    该研究表明，工具接口表示会改变智能体的动作选择、失败、恢复和后续轨迹，并提出了一种能够提升性能、降低成本的修复方法。这是关于智能体接口与交互的核心系统贡献；其决策行为分析与推理有一定关联，但没有研究模型内部机制或组合泛化。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Language agents increasingly act through external tools and interactive environments, making the interface between the model and its executable capabilities part of the decision process. Model Context Protocol (MCP) and command-line interfaces (CLI) can expose the same semantic operations through markedly different model-facing representations. We study whether these representational differences change agent behavior when executable capabilities are matched. We introduce Matched Interface Comparison and Analysis (MICA), which renders MCP and CLI from a shared semantic action contract and routes decoded actions through the same runtime. Across six models and three interactive environments, matched interfaces produce substantial differences in task performance and interaction cost. These effects extend beyond surface validity to semantic action selection, failure pathways, and recovery. Matched-state probes localize sensitivity to capability presentation, realization, and feedback. Paired natural trajectories reveal structured divergence in 94.3% of 2,004 episodes and show that early differences propagate through subsequent interaction. This analysis identifies interface realization as a direct intervention boundary. We therefore introduce Decoupled Action Realization and Targeted Repair (DART), which preserves validated semantic commitments while repairing interface-specific realization. DART improves benchmark score in all six evaluated settings by up to 9.0 points and reduces MCP token cost in all three environments by up to 27.1k tokens per task. Together, these results establish interface representation as part of the closed-loop decision environment shaping agent behavior.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Understanding how individual token choices affect reasoning length is important for characterizing reasoning models. Building on prior findings that changing the first reasoning token (hereafter, the first token) can substantially alter reasoning length, we focus on this initial choice to investigate how its influence operates during subsequent generation. One possibility is that the first token changes the early text that follows, which in turn affects reasoning length. However, replacing only the first token of an existing reasoning prefix and resuming generation substantially changes the remaining reasoning length, even though all other prefix tokens are unchanged. To trace this persistent influence, we compare next-token distributions while varying only the first token and find that sensitivity is concentrated at a small set of generation positions. Blocking attention from these positions to the first token reduces the length gap between first-token conditions. Using next-token distributions from a different first-token condition at these positions also substantially changes subsequent reasoning length. Together, these findings suggest that attention to the first token at a few sensitive positions helps sustain its length effect, illustrating how a local token choice persistently influences a sequence-level outcome.

    Yalun Wu, Qiwei Ma, Bingbing Xu, Dan Zhang, Long Bai, Boyang Wang, Jiatong Li, Zheqi Lv, Shaozu Yuan, Peiying Wang, Jiawei Wang, An Zhang, Tat-Seng Chua

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    EvolveMAS centers on decentralized agents adapting across episodes through governed memory and reusable interaction knowledge, with benchmark and ablation evidence for the framework. Its agent and memory architecture is a core Systems contribution; reuse across settings is only incidental to compositional generalization, and the abstract does not study internal model mechanisms or reasoning capabilities.

    EvolveMAS 的核心是去中心化智能体通过受管理的记忆和可复用的交互知识跨回合适应，并提供了基准和消融实验作为框架有效性的证据。其智能体和记忆架构是系统领域的核心贡献；跨设置重用与组合泛化的关联只是附带的，摘要也没有研究模型内部机制或推理能力。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Decentralized multi-agent systems (MAS) enable large language model agents to interact without centralized control. Agents need to adapt to other agents at test time and reuse accumulated experience to refine their interaction strategies for future interactions across cooperative, mixed-motive, and adversarial settings. However, existing approaches often develop adaptation mechanisms for particular interaction settings. This raises a central question: how can decentralized MAS support test-time adaptation and reliable experience reuse across interaction settings? We propose EvolveMAS, a unified self-evolution framework that supports experience-driven adaptation within and across episodes. EvolveMAS pairs each main agent with a dedicated MemoryAgent for test-time memory governance, which maintains isolated Structured Memory outside the main agent's reasoning context. EvolveMAS organizes adaptation into two complementary processes: Within-Episode Online Adaptation and Cross-Episode Knowledge Evolution. During Within-Episode Online Adaptation, MemoryAgent updates episodic, semantic, and working memory from interaction evidence to inform subsequent actions. During Cross-Episode Knowledge Evolution, the main agent uses memory and episode outcomes to distill reusable interaction knowledge comprising partner profiles and interaction strategies for subsequent episodes. Across five benchmarks and six evaluation configurations spanning the three interaction settings, EvolveMAS achieves the highest normalized average score of 77.2 among the compared methods. Ablations show that test-time memory governance and cross-episode knowledge reuse both improve performance. Interaction traces further illustrate how updated memory and distilled knowledge guide subsequent interactions. These results support experience-driven adaptation in decentralized MAS without updating model parameters.

    去中心化多智能体系统（MAS）使大语言模型智能体能够在没有集中控制的情况下进行交互。智能体需要在测试时适应其他智能体，并重用积累的经验来完善交互策略，以便在合作、混合动机和对抗等设置中进行后续交互。然而，现有方法往往针对特定交互设置开发适应机制。这引出了一个核心问题：去中心化 MAS 如何支持测试时适应，并在不同交互设置之间可靠地重用经验？我们提出 EvolveMAS，这是一种统一的自演化框架，支持在单回合内及跨回合进行经验驱动的适应。EvolveMAS 为每个主智能体配备专用的 MemoryAgent，用于测试时的记忆管理；MemoryAgent 在主智能体推理上下文之外维护相互隔离的结构化记忆。EvolveMAS 将适应组织为两个互补过程：回合内在线适应和跨回合知识演化。在回合内在线适应过程中，MemoryAgent 根据交互证据更新情景记忆、语义记忆和工作记忆，以指导后续行动。在跨回合知识演化过程中，主智能体利用记忆和回合结果，提炼可复用的交互知识，包括伙伴画像和后续回合使用的交互策略。在涵盖三种交互设置的五个基准和六种评估配置中，EvolveMAS 在所比较的方法中取得了最高的归一化平均分 77.2。消融实验表明，测试时记忆管理和跨回合知识重用均能提升性能。交互轨迹进一步展示了更新后的记忆和提炼出的知识如何指导后续交互。这些结果表明，在不更新模型参数的情况下，去中心化 MAS 可以实现经验驱动的适应。

    Yichuan Chen, Xin Wang

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper analyzes how memory-store size harms proactive recall and contributes a false-alarm scaling analysis and a label-free conformal gate. This directly advances memory use in long-lived assistants; the decision process has only an incidental connection to reasoning capabilities.

    本文分析了记忆存储规模如何损害主动召回，并提出了误报率随规模变化的分析以及一种无需标签的保形门控器。这项工作直接推动了长期助手对记忆的运用；其决策过程与推理能力仅有间接关联。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    A long-lived assistant that brings up memories without being asked must decide at every turn whether anything in its store is worth an interruption. We show that this decision is a multiple-testing problem whose difficulty grows with the store size $N$. On streaming replays of LongMemEval and LoCoMo, a similarity threshold tuned to 5% false alarms at $N=8$ reaches 87-100% at $N=2048$, across embedding models and for explicit and implicit cues; LLM judges show the same growth from a lower base. We prove that a gate with false-alarm rate $\alpha$ operates at a per-item false-positive rate of about $-\ln(1-\alpha)/N$, which pins its hit rate to the far left of the single-comparison ROC curve and, under regular variation, makes it decay as a power of $N$ with an explicit constant. The resulting prediction matches the hit rate of a per-$N$ oracle threshold to within one percentage point. The analysis explains why lexical and semantic channels need thresholds growing like $\ln N$ and $\sqrt{\ln N}$, and why per-cue normalisation roughly doubles the hit rate at matched false alarms. A cue-swap conformal gate, which compares the current cue with the user's other cues on the same store, needs no labels and has a finite-sample false-alarm guarantee under exchangeability; on LongMemEval it holds false alarms near 5% at the hit rate of a label-tuned threshold. Three annotators (Fleiss' $\kappa=0.63$) find that about nine in ten false alarms are genuine interruptions. Code and data: https://github.com/RiverChenStillCompiling/price-of-scale

    中文

    一个会在用户未提出请求时主动提起记忆的长期助手，必须在每一轮判断其存储中的内容是否值得打断用户。我们表明，这一判断属于多重检验问题，其难度会随着存储规模的扩大而增加 $N$。在 LongMemEval 和 LoCoMo 的流式重放中，将相似度阈值调至在 $N=8$ 时误报率为 5%，在 $N=2048$ 时误报率会升至 87%–100%；这一现象在不同嵌入模型以及显式和隐式线索下均成立。LLM 评判器也呈现相同的增长趋势，但起点较低。我们证明，误报率为 $\alpha$ 的门控器，其单项假阳性率约为 $-\ln(1-\alpha)/N$，这会使其命中率落在单次比较 ROC 曲线的最左端；在正则变差条件下，命中率会按 $N$ 的幂次衰减，且常数项有显式表达式。由此得到的预测，与逐 $N$ 的 oracle 阈值所达到的命中率相差不超过一个百分点。该分析解释了为何词汇和语义通道的阈值分别需要按 $\ln N$ 和 $\sqrt{\ln N}$ 增长，也解释了为何在误报率相同的情况下，按线索归一化大致能使命中率翻倍。线索交换保形门控器会将当前线索与同一存储中该用户的其他线索进行比较，无需标签，并且在可交换性假设下具有有限样本误报保证；在 LongMemEval 上，其误报率维持在约 5%，同时命中率达到标签调优阈值的水平。三位标注者（Fleiss' $\kappa=0.63$）发现，约十分之九的误报确实会打断用户。代码和数据：https://github.com/RiverChenStillCompiling/price-of-scale

    将智能体记忆视为推荐：用于大语言模型智能体长期记忆的推荐系统设计

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper formalizes LLM agent memory selection as budgeted slate recommendation and develops a call-free method that improves multi-session retrieval accuracy and serving cost. Memory and agent architecture are central; recommendation’s selection of multiple memories is only an incidental connection to compositionality, and the abstract makes no claim about reasoning mechanisms or internal representations.

    本文将大语言模型智能体的记忆选择形式化为预算约束下的列表式推荐，并开发出一种无需调用 LLM、能提升多会话检索准确率并降低服务成本的方法。记忆和智能体架构是核心内容；多条记忆的推荐选择与组合性仅有附带关联，摘要也未对推理机制或内部表征提出主张。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large language model (LLM) agents that serve users across many sessions must choose, for every request, the few stored memories that enter a limited context window. This choice largely decides whether the agent answers correctly, and it runs on every request at Web scale. This selection faces three challenges: a large and growing store, a per-request cost budget, and multi-session questions that need all of their evidence. Many memory systems build notes or graphs with hundreds to thousands of LLM calls per history, and each is designed on its own, so it is unclear which component yields the accuracy. These challenges mirror the properties of recommendation, so we formalize agent memory as budgeted slate recommendation, with the request as the user, stored memories as items and the context window as a slate. The formalization places memory systems in one design space of recommender cascades and factorizes accuracy into the completeness that each stage controls. Guided by it, we propose AgentMemRec, which adapts candidate generation, learning to rank and slate construction from recommender systems and selects memories without any LLM call. On multi-session questions of LongMemEval, AgentMemRec outperforms memory and context-selection methods, including A-Mem, HippoRAG 2, DynamicRAG and T-Mem, by 10 to 31 points of accuracy. It matches an LLM reranker that makes 64 calls per query at 3.2 times lower serving cost, and on LoCoMo it outperforms Mem0 and Zep without any LLM call at write time. The factorization attributes the gains to slates that more often hold all of the evidence, so recommender-system design offers an effective and efficient foundation for the long-term memory of LLM agents.

    Luise Ge, Brendan Juba

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper develops query-driven lifted reasoning, including a bounded-concealment condition, an algorithm, and soundness, completeness, and efficiency guarantees. Its focus is formal reasoning; lifted structure and agent motivation do not establish a substantive contribution to composition or agent systems.

    本文发展了查询驱动的提升式推理，提出有界隐匿性条件和算法，并给出可靠性、完备性和效率保证。论文聚焦于形式推理；提升结构和对智能体的动机并不能证明其对组合或智能体系统作出了实质贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Learning and reasoning are both essential to intelligent agents, but have traditionally been treated as two separate stages: first learning a knowledge base from data (or taking one as given), and then verifying queries as if the knowledge base were complete. This separation has been shown to be inefficient when the downstream goal is to verify only a small set of queries. Moreover, it neglects the possibility that data and a knowledge base contain partial yet complementary information, requiring an agent to combine both sources to justify or refute a query. Motivated by the need to integrate learning and reasoning more tightly, we study the problem of query-driven learning for reasoning. More specifically, we extend prior work to the first-order setting, which is critical for practical applications as the number of ground atoms typically grows rapidly. We begin by asking when validating or refuting a universal query given partial data and knowledge base is even possible, and identify a necessary and sufficient condition called bounded concealment. We then propose a quasi-polynomial-time algorithm that solves the task at the lifted level. Finally, we establish soundness and completeness guarantees relative to space-bounded lifted proofs, along with quasipolynomial sample and runtime bounds, demonstrating that lifted query-driven reasoning can be efficient even when unrestricted knowledge-base learning is not.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper directly analyzes LoRA’s internal component and layer effects using mechanistic interpretability, then uses those findings to select task-specific adaptation layers. Reasoning tasks serve as evaluation settings, while the method concerns fine-tuning efficiency rather than reasoning mechanisms or system computation.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has emerged as the dominant paradigm for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models. Standard all-layer LoRA applies adaptation throughout the transformer, despite heterogeneous contributions from its components. In this work, we conduct a systematic mechanistic interpretability analysis to understand how LoRA affects model internals. We observe that LoRA's adaptation effect is highly non-uniform, with significant component-wise and layer-wise sparsity. Most critically, we find that important layers are highly task-dependent, with limited overlap across tasks. Motivated by these insights, we propose Adaptive-LoRA, a calibration-driven method that automatically identifies task-specific layers via frozen-base zero-ablation, enabling efficient layer selection without exhaustive search. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-1.5B across 11 diverse reasoning tasks demonstrate that Adaptive-LoRA outperforms full-layer LoRA while using only 30% of layers, achieving a $3.5\times$ reduction in adapter parameters. This work bridges mechanistic interpretability and practical efficiency, providing both fundamental insights and a principled approach for adaptive fine-tuning.

    Mohamed Elsayed, Minh Pham, A. Rupam Mahmood

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    SRM introduces a recurrent state for streaming learning that supports content- or time-based recall, delayed feedback, and order-dependent transformations, evaluated on memory and control tasks. These capabilities touch composition and learning, but its central contribution is a model memory system, rather than interpretability or reasoning mechanisms.

    SRM 提出一种用于流式学习的循环状态，支持按内容或时间回忆、处理延迟反馈以及执行与输入顺序相关的变换，并在记忆和控制任务上进行评估。这些能力涉及组合与学习，但其核心贡献是模型记忆系统，而非可解释性或推理机制。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Natural intelligence learns from a continuous stream of sensorimotor experience: data can arrive at high bandwidth, and behavior adapts to feedback as soon as it arrives, even when it is delayed. In contrast, most modern deep learning systems rely on stored datasets, replay buffers, and retained contexts through which credit is later assigned. At high data rates, storing and revisiting past experience can be impractical under tight memory and computational constraints. This paper studies recurrent memory under a streaming learning constraint: the learner learns from experience as soon as it arrives without storing raw experience. We ask whether a streaming learner can maintain a state that remains useful for future prediction and control from delayed feedback. We introduce Streaming Recurrent Memory (SRM), a recurrent memory designed for the streaming setting which preserves information that may matter later while remaining trainable with one-step backpropagation through time (BPTT). SRM provides a streaming-compatible recurrence that is designed to recall past information by content or time, track elapsed steps, and compose transformations whose outcome depends on the order in which inputs are observed. Across controlled memory tasks and streaming applications, SRM learns effectively with one-step BPTT, outperforming recurrent baselines in associative recall and online language modeling while achieving near-perfect success in associative T-Maze with delayed rewards. These results suggest that fixing how inputs are stored in the recurrent state, while learning how that state is read out, enables effective streaming learning without long-range backpropagation.

    自然智能从连续的感觉运动经验流中学习：数据可以高速到达，行为会在反馈到达后立即适应，即使反馈有所延迟也是如此。相比之下，现代深度学习系统大多依赖存储的数据集、回放缓冲区和保留的上下文，之后再通过这些内容分配信用。在数据速率较高且内存和计算资源受限时，存储并重新访问过去的经验可能并不现实。本文研究流式学习约束下的循环记忆：学习者在经验到达时立即学习，而不存储原始经验。我们探讨流式学习者能否维护一种状态，使其在收到延迟反馈时仍能用于未来的预测和控制。我们提出流式循环记忆（SRM），一种专为流式场景设计的循环记忆，它保留以后可能有用的信息，同时仍可通过单步时间反向传播（BPTT）进行训练。SRM 提供一种兼容流式处理的循环机制，旨在按内容或时间回忆过去信息、跟踪经过的步数，并组合其结果取决于输入观测顺序的变换。在受控记忆任务和流式应用中，SRM 能够通过单步 BPTT 有效学习；它在联想回忆和在线语言建模方面优于循环基线，并在带延迟奖励的联想 T-Maze 任务中取得近乎完美的成功率。这些结果表明，固定输入存入循环状态的方式，同时学习如何读取该状态，可以在不进行长程反向传播的情况下实现有效的流式学习。

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The framework uses executable physics worlds, counterfactual tasks, and verifier feedback to train VLMs for causal physical reasoning, with transfer to unseen dynamics; reasoning is its central contribution.     ENGLISH

    Physical reasoning underpins how embodied systems understand and act in the physical world, yet vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable on questions about dynamics and physical causality. Progress is critically constrained by the scarcity of grounded counterfactual training data, as observational videos capture only the factual trajectory that occurred. The self-evolving paradigm offers a route beyond fixed datasets by enabling models to construct their own training problems. Extending this paradigm to physics, however, requires an external source of truth that can both validate model-proposed environments and verify alternative physical outcomes under intervention. We introduce \physevolve{}, a verifier-grounded self-evolving framework that trains VLMs for causal physical reasoning from model-proposed executable worlds and simulation-authored tasks. At each round, a shared VLM proposes executable world programs and evidence schemas; a deterministic physics engine freezes each valid world, simulates matched baseline and body-elided counterfactual branches, and synthesizes discrete, answer-bound visual tasks. Exact verifier feedback from task solving updates both the shared policy via GRPO and an adaptive curriculum over physical intents. Starting from Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, \physevolve{} achieves targeted gains across PhysBench, CausalPhys, and ContPhy without human intervention data, improving PhysBench Throwing by $8.8$ points and ContPhy Counterfactual Removal and Goal-Pit by $7.4$ and $24.4$ points. These gains concentrate on interaction-sensitive and altered-world questions, demonstrating zero-shot transfer of causal principles to unseen complex dynamics (cloth, fluid, soft bodies) and real-world video.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The study identifies recurring patterns in coding-model reasoning traces and tests their use for prompting and early stopping, directly addressing reasoning behavior and its control. Trace analysis offers limited insight into observable behavior, but does not establish internal mechanisms; token reduction through early stopping is incidental to the systems interests.

    该研究识别了编码模型推理轨迹中反复出现的模式，并测试了将其用于提示和提前停止的效果，直接探讨了推理行为及其控制。轨迹分析只能有限地揭示可观察行为，并不能确定内部机制；通过提前停止减少 token 用量，与系统领域的关联较弱。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) generate long reasoning traces that expose intermediate inference behavior, offering opportunities to study and control reasoning in AI coding. However, the underlying patterns in these traces and their potential for analyzing and guiding coding models remain poorly understood, limiting systematic characterization and inference-time control of LRM reasoning. We conduct an empirical study of reasoning patterns across four representative coding tasks. We transform reasoning traces into structured action sequences and mine recurring fragments using within-task support, cross-task contrasts, and valid--invalid support contrasts. We characterize four general reasoning patterns by coding agents: design-to-implementation for code generation, state tracing for execution reasoning, evidence--fix--recheck for debugging, and semantic mapping for translation. We further identify positive and negative patterns associated with valid and invalid reasoning traces, respectively. Positive patterns reflect verification-driven convergence, whereas negative patterns reflect repeated design revision, reflection, and knowledge recall without closure. To demonstrate their practical utility, we evaluate three pattern-based applications: task identification, pattern-guided prompting, and pattern-aware early stopping. Features capturing general reasoning patterns enable accurate task identification from reasoning traces without accessing task descriptions or final answers. Prompting guided by positive and negative patterns improves the overall accuracy of downstream tasks, while negative pattern-aware early stopping substantially reduces API-reported token usage with only a modest decrease in pass@1. All three applications also generalize to previously unseen models, showing that reasoning patterns can support both the analysis and control of LRM behavior in AI coding.

    大型推理模型（LRM）会生成很长的推理轨迹，揭示中间推断行为，为研究和控制 AI 编码中的推理提供了机会。然而，这些轨迹中潜藏的模式及其在分析和引导编码模型方面的潜力仍鲜为人知，限制了对 LRM 推理进行系统刻画和推理时控制。我们针对四种有代表性的编码任务，对推理模式开展实证研究。我们将推理轨迹转换为结构化动作序列，并通过任务内支持度、跨任务对比以及有效与无效轨迹之间的支持度对比，挖掘反复出现的片段。我们归纳出编码智能体的四种通用推理模式：代码生成中的从设计到实现、执行推理中的状态追踪、调试中的证据—修复—复查，以及翻译中的语义映射。我们还分别识别出与有效和无效推理轨迹相关的正向与负向模式。正向模式体现了由验证驱动的收敛，而负向模式则表现为反复修改设计、反思和回忆知识，却始终未能得出结论。为展示这些模式的实际效用，我们评估了三种基于模式的应用：任务识别、模式引导提示和模式感知提前停止。提取通用推理模式的特征后，无需访问任务描述或最终答案，即可根据推理轨迹准确识别任务。由正向与负向模式引导的提示能够提高下游任务的总体准确率，而针对负向模式的提前停止则大幅降低 API 报告的 token 用量，同时仅使 pass@1 略有下降。这三种应用也都能泛化到此前未见过的模型，表明推理模式既可用于分析，也可用于控制 AI 编码中的 LRM 行为。

    A dot product means something only when both vectors share a coordinate system. Content words have one; a fresh entity does not: rotating its coordinates alone changes nothing. We take this per-entity frame freedom as a symmetry and ask what it forces in attention. For orthogonal transports, invariant scores depend only on norms and the transported inner product $\langle x_i,T_{ij}x_j\rangle$; equivariant messages lie in the span of $x_i$ and $T_{ij}x_j$. Endpoint channel count bounds transport rank, so with one vector per entity relations must be supplied; standard attention is the flat sector of a shared frame. Representation theory attaches an integer to each mechanism; the readout decides which. With orthogonal transitions, a convex-cell readout composes a finite group exactly only at or above its smallest faithful real representation dimension. At this minimum, exactness forces a faithful representation. An even readout can decode a cover at smaller width, and the gap is unbounded. Below its threshold, the part of the group a mechanism cannot see sets an accuracy ceiling computable before training. 17/17 fitting seeds at minimal width passed tests through length 1000, versus 7/18 at twice the width; 12 models carry correctness certificates to explicit lengths, from the weights alone. On $C_3\times A_4$ (faithful width 5), descent at width 4 learned the 72-state double cover under sign-blind attention (6/48 seeds; monotone 0/48); on a frozen cover the cross-entropy-optimal affine head is uniform, a quadratic head exact. On parsed CLUTRR, transported composition beats a matched transformer by 41 points at 4-10 hops, but forcing isometries costs 65 points; on StepGame's commutative algebra, isometries help.     Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    Info-GRPO changes how reasoning models explore by correlating latent seeds with whole reasoning trajectories, and the abstract reports gains on reasoning benchmarks.     Info-GRPO 通过将潜在种子与完整推理轨迹相关联，改变了推理模型的探索方式；摘要报告了其在推理基准上的性能提升。轨迹级多样性与组合的关联有限，而模型训练和策略探索本身并不能构成系统方面的贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Reasoning models trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) now produce chains of thought thousands of tokens long, and recent studies reveal that such training is prone to policy collapse. Entropy regularization is the standard remedy, but it works by pushing probability mass away from the few tokens that carry it and toward the vast low-probability tail of the vocabulary, and it applies this force once for every token of the reasoning trace. This puts the bonus in direct conflict with the entropy decay that convergence requires, and makes its coefficient difficult to set in the long-trace regime. To resolve this tension, we propose Info-GRPO, an information-theoretic framework that cultivates correlation between the policy and a latent prior. Rather than raising entropy everywhere, Info-GRPO builds on the mutual information between a latent variable and the trajectory it induces: augmenting prompts with latent seeds during training lets the model explore diverse policies correlated with the prior, while the seed-conditioned entropy is guided toward convergence. Diversity is therefore carried across whole reasoning traces rather than by per-token randomness, and exploration no longer fights entropy reduction. Experiments show that Info-GRPO outperforms vanilla GRPO and entropy-regularized GRPO across diverse reasoning benchmarks. On AIME24, it improves $Avg@8$ over GRPO by 3.75%, 1.66%, 4.16%, and 4.17% on four backbones, and it reaches the same majority-vote accuracy with $8\times$ fewer samples. Code and models will be publicly released.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    ENGLISH

    Recent methods for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) use rollout diversity to improve reasoning performance or training efficiency. Despite these gains, the extent to which differences among correct-answer rollouts reflect useful alternative reasoning or unresolved errors remains poorly understood. We investigate this question through a blind paired analysis of a model trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), comparing the highest- and lowest-agreement correct-answer traces for the same problem. Across 126 pairs, low-agreement traces have more spurious reasoning than high-agreement traces (35% vs. 22%), including internal inconsistencies and misuse of problem conditions. Based on these findings, we propose RoAR (Rollout-Agreement Reward), which adds reasoning-level agreement to GRPO's rewards for verified-correct rollouts. RoAR computes this signal from existing on-policy rollout groups, requiring no human-written rationales, additional sampling, or separately trained process evaluator. On five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, the 1.5B GRPO-RoAR model reaches 55.5% mean pass@1 under zero-shot evaluation using 7K training examples, exceeding GRPO and GRPO-CARE by 6.0 and 5.5 percentage points. A separate blind audit of 100 problems answered correctly by all four 1.5B models finds spurious rates of 18% for GRPO-RoAR, 32% for GRPO, 27% for GRPO-CARE, and 37% for DRA-GRPO. Our findings identify reasoning validity as an important consideration when using rollout differences to guide learning. Our code is available at https://github.com/ldi-kyunghee/RoAR.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    GUI agents built on vision-language models interact with continuously evolving interfaces, yet conventional inference repeatedly recomputes representations of largely overlapping observations and histories. This mismatch makes multi-step interaction costly, while changes in context, interface content, and action arguments prevent straightforward cache reuse. We introduce GUIFlow, a framework for full-pipeline incremental inference in multi-image GUI interaction. Our central insight is that advancing a decision need not require rebuilding all supporting representations: each interaction step can instead selectively update computational states maintained across the trajectory. To support new decisions as the context evolves, GUIFlow adapts how past computation is reused: historical KV states are position-aligned and injected into the current context; change signals guide selective updates of current-observation states in the vision encoder and language model; and earlier action responses serve as speculative drafts verified by the target model. Together, these mechanisms enable cross-step reuse throughout visual encoding, prefill, and decoding without additional training, a separate draft model, or changes to the model-visible inputs and action interface. Experiments demonstrate up to 3.39x geometric-mean speedup across offline multi-image benchmarks and up to 3.49x in online, closed-loop interaction on OSWorld, while maintaining task performance broadly comparable to the dense baseline.

AMIE distils a semantic teacher's keep/suppress judgments into a retrieval-conditioned policy and accumulates its selective actions into bounded state that reweights subsequent host retrievals. Surprisingly, even a zero-call policy that simply accumulates retrieval frequency can match or outperform semantic policies in several settings, revealing retrieval traffic itself as a strong signal for access adaptation, while learned selectivity improves robustness when frequently retrieved memories remain useful.     Large language models (LLMs) now serve as the backbone of agents that reason over many turns, call tools, and pursue long-horizon tasks. To avoid recomputation, a model stores the attention keys and values of all past tokens in a key-value (KV) cache. Each layer maintains its own cache, so KV-cache memory can become the main bottleneck for GPU serving. Most compression methods operate within a single layer, by quantizing the cache entries, reducing the channel dimension, or evicting less important tokens. All three lose substantial accuracy at high compression ratios. Cross-layer methods share one compressed cache across adjacent layers to go beyond this limit. However, these methods also degrade sharply at high compression ratios. We find that the KV-cache representations of adjacent layers are quite different, whereas the input hidden states of adjacent layers are highly similar. We also find that, under the same memory budget, reducing the dimension of this shared latent loses far more accuracy than quantizing it. Based on these findings, we propose BellowsKV, a training-free method that maps the hidden states of n adjacent layers to one shared latent per token. At inference time, each layer reads its own keys and values from this latent through a layer-specific projection. We keep the latent at full dimension and compress it in two other ways: BellowsKV-Quant stores the latent at low precision, which is nearly lossless because the latent has no dominant outlier channels; BellowsKV-Evict makes one shared eviction decision per block, because the layers rank token importance very similarly. Across Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B and Qwen2.5-7B, BellowsKV-Quant retains about 99% of full-cache accuracy at 3.6x compression and 97-98% at 13-14x, where the strongest cross-layer method retains at most 84% at 16x. Code: https://github.com/MorrisZJ/BellowsKV

    中文

    大型语言模型（LLM）如今已成为智能体的核心，使其能够进行多轮推理、调用工具并执行长时程任务。为避免重复计算，模型会将所有过去 token 的注意力键和值存储在键值（KV）缓存中。每一层都维护自己的缓存，因此 KV 缓存可能成为 GPU 服务中的主要瓶颈。大多数压缩方法在单层内操作，包括量化缓存条目、缩减通道维度或淘汰不太重要的 token。这三种方法在高压缩率下都会造成显著的准确率损失。跨层方法在相邻层之间共享一个压缩缓存，以突破这一限制。然而，这些方法在高压缩率下也会急剧退化。我们发现，相邻层的 KV 缓存表示差异很大，而相邻层的输入隐藏状态则高度相似。我们还发现，在相同内存预算下，缩减这一共享潜变量的维度所造成的准确率损失远大于对其进行量化。基于这些发现，我们提出 BellowsKV，这是一种无需训练的方法，将 n 个相邻层的隐藏状态映射到每个 token 的一个共享潜变量。推理时，每一层通过特定于该层的投影，从这一潜变量中读取自己的键和值。我们保留潜变量的完整维度，并通过另外两种方式对其压缩：BellowsKV-Quant 以低精度存储潜变量，由于潜变量没有占主导地位的异常值通道，因此几乎无损；BellowsKV-Evict 则在每个块上作出一个共享的淘汰决策，因为各层对 token 重要性的排序非常相似。在 Llama-3.1-8B、Mistral-7B 和 Qwen2.5-7B 上，BellowsKV-Quant 在 3.6 倍压缩下保留了约 99% 的全缓存准确率，在 13–14 倍压缩下保留了 97–98%；而在 16 倍压缩下，最强的跨层方法至多保留 84%。代码：https://github.com/MorrisZJ/BellowsKV

    S3AC：面向 LLM 推理的稳定、选择性与可扩展演员-评论家

    Shuo Shen, Guangran Cheng, Chengqi Lyu, Xiangsen Wang, Yanan Sun, Wenwei Zhang

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    S3AC trains a critic for token-level credit assignment in long-CoT RLVR and uses critic-based difficulty estimates to select prompts, directly targeting reasoning training and efficiency. The actor-critic and prompt-selection design substantially advances model training systems, while the abstract offers no contribution to interpretability or compositional generalization.

    S3AC 为长 CoT 的 RLVR 训练评论家以实现词元级信用分配，并使用基于评论家的难度估计来选择提示，直接针对推理训练和效率。其演员-评论家与提示选择设计实质性地推进了模型训练系统，但摘要未涉及可解释性或组合泛化方面的贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Critic-free methods are widely used in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, avoiding difficult and costly critic training. Common alternatives lack token-level credit assignment and typically rely on grouped rollouts to estimate prompt-specific baselines. A critic can address both limitations, but long-CoT critic training is hindered by insufficient coverage of trajectories with diverse lengths and early gradients dominated by the newly initialized value head. We introduce S3AC (Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic) for LLM reasoning, built around a practical critic-training recipe. The trained critic provides token-specific advantages and prompt-specific baselines. Using the prompt-level baseline to estimate difficulty, we propose Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling (DAPS). DAPS combines this estimate with outcome history to select prompts before generation, reducing rollout waste without offline difficulty initialization. S3AC improves group-rollout performance across dense and mixture-of-experts models from 1.5B to 397B parameters, outperforming a modern GRPO variant (GRPO-X). At 35B, it sustains single-rollout training while tested critic-free baselines deteriorate after initial gains.

    中文

    在用于长链式思维（CoT）推理的可验证奖励强化学习（RLVR）中，无评论家方法被广泛采用，以避免困难且成本高昂的评论家训练。常见替代方法缺少词元级信用分配，通常依赖分组采样来估计特定提示的基线。评论家可以同时解决这两个局限，但长 CoT 评论家训练会受到不同长度轨迹覆盖不足的影响，而且训练初期的梯度会被新初始化的价值头所主导。我们提出面向 LLM 推理的 S3AC（稳定、选择性与可扩展的演员-评论家），其核心是一套实用的评论家训练方案。训练好的评论家可提供特定词元的优势值和特定提示的基线。我们利用提示级基线估计难度，并提出难度感知提示采样（DAPS）。DAPS 将该估计与结果历史相结合，在生成前选择提示，无需离线初始化难度即可减少采样浪费。S3AC 在从 1.5B 到 397B 参数的稠密模型和混合专家模型上提升了分组采样表现，优于一种现代 GRPO 变体（GRPO-X）。在 35B 规模下，它能够维持单次采样训练，而经过测试的无评论家基线在初步提升后表现退化。

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    EvoRouter trains a routing policy through insight-guided on-policy distillation and cost-aware reinforcement learning, using execution feedback to improve multi-agent configuration decisions. This substantially advances agent organization and resource allocation, with a meaningful but secondary contribution to planning and reasoning; it does not study internal representations.

    EvoRouter 通过洞见引导的在策略蒸馏和成本感知强化学习来训练路由策略，利用执行反馈改进多智能体配置决策。这显著推进了智能体组织和资源分配，对规划和推理也有重要但次要的贡献；它没有研究内部表征。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Serving web queries at scale with multi-agent systems requires jointly configuring large language models, collaboration modes, agent counts, interaction rounds, and skills. However, the resulting configuration space grows combinatorially, while sparse execution rewards provide limited fine-grained supervision for interdependent planning decisions. We propose EvoRouter, a self-evolving multi-agent routing framework driven by insight-guided on-policy distillation. A dedicated expert periodically synthesizes performance-cost feedback from configuration trajectories across tasks into reusable conditional routing insights about capability requirements, returns from resource scaling, and interactions among configuration choices. A privileged teacher combines these evolving insights with current execution feedback to provide dense token-level supervision for the router's own planning trajectories through on-policy distillation. Cost-aware reinforcement learning jointly optimizes task performance and computational cost. Together, these training signals internalize execution insights into the routing policy. The updated policy generates new trajectories that support subsequent insight extraction, forming an execution-driven self-improvement loop. We evaluate EvoRouter on 19 in-domain datasets spanning five domains and two out-of-domain benchmarks. EvoRouter achieves an average in-domain accuracy of 68.69%, outperforming the strongest routing baseline by 7.23 percentage points while reducing inference compute cost by 50.95%. Our code is open-sourced at https://github.com/CenYangtze/EvoRouter.

    中文

    使用多智能体系统大规模提供网络查询服务，需要联合配置大型语言模型、协作模式、智能体数量、交互轮数和技能。然而，由此产生的配置空间呈组合式增长，而稀疏的执行奖励无法为相互依赖的规划决策提供足够细粒度的监督。我们提出 EvoRouter，这是一个由洞见引导的在策略蒸馏驱动的自进化多智能体路由框架。一个专门的专家会定期将跨任务配置轨迹中的性能—成本反馈，综合为可复用的条件路由洞见，涉及能力需求、资源扩展的收益以及配置选择之间的相互作用。一个特权教师将这些不断演化的洞见与当前执行反馈结合，通过在策略蒸馏，为路由器自身的规划轨迹提供密集的逐词元监督。成本感知强化学习则联合优化任务表现和计算成本。这些训练信号共同使路由策略内化执行洞见。更新后的策略会生成新的轨迹，以支持后续洞见提取，从而形成由执行驱动的自我改进循环。我们在涵盖五个领域的 19 个域内数据集以及两个域外基准上评估 EvoRouter。EvoRouter 的域内平均准确率达到 68.69%，比表现最强的路由基线高 7.23 个百分点，同时将推理计算成本降低 50.95%。我们的代码已在 https://github.com/CenYangtze/EvoRouter 开源。

    Zhengping Jiang, William Jurayj, Liaoyaqi Wang, Chunsheng Zuo, Anqi Liu, Benjamin Van Durme

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    FOCUS uses selective branching to improve critic learning and credit assignment for long-horizon agent reinforcement learning, with gains on reasoning and other benchmarks; its central contribution directly advances training for multi-step problem solving. Its context-management interface and rollout allocation also make a substantial systems contribution, while segment boundaries alone do not establish compositional generalization.

    FOCUS通过选择性分支改进长时程智能体强化学习中的评论器学习和信用分配，并在推理及其他基准上取得提升；其核心贡献直接推动了多步问题求解训练。其上下文管理接口和轨迹展开分配也构成了重要的系统贡献，而片段边界本身并不能证明组合泛化能力。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Sparse outcome rewards make it difficult for long-horizon language-model agents to assign credit to earlier actions. Learned critics provide value estimates for intermediate states, but these estimates can be inaccurate, while estimating intermediate values with repetitive continuation samples from points within a trajectory incurs substantial costs. To mitigate these issues, we introduce FOCUS, an RL method that uses selective branching to help the critic network learn its value estimator. The rollout controller facilitates active learning for the critic by sampling continuations from states that are expected to most reduce the critic's estimation error. These refined value estimates then score the segment between consecutive states with a TD($\lambda$) advantage, while the sampled evidence supplies training targets for the critic. FOCUS supports long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning through a modular context-management interface that decouples context management from rollout allocation. Our experiments show that using compaction-induced segment boundaries for value estimation and credit assignment, FOCUS outperforms GRPO and VinePPO with matched per-step generation budgets on legal reasoning, deep search, and code localization benchmarks, improving held-out accuracy at Qwen3.5-9B scale by 7.2 points over the strongest baseline on BrowseComp-Plus (55.4 vs. 48.2) and by 4.1 points on DeonticBench (56.5 vs. 52.4).

    中文

    稀疏的结果奖励使长时程语言模型智能体难以将功劳归于较早的动作。学习得到的评论器可为中间状态提供价值估计，但这些估计可能不准确；而从轨迹中的各个点反复采样后续过程来估计中间价值，成本又很高。为缓解这些问题，我们提出FOCUS，这是一种使用选择性分支来帮助评论器网络学习其价值估计器的RL方法。轨迹展开控制器通过从预期最能降低评论器估计误差的状态采样后续过程，促进评论器的主动学习。随后，这些经过改进的价值估计会通过TD($\lambda$)优势为连续状态之间的片段打分，而采样得到的证据则为评论器提供训练目标。FOCUS通过模块化的上下文管理接口支持长时程智能体强化学习，该接口将上下文管理与轨迹展开分配解耦。实验表明，使用由上下文压缩引出的片段边界进行价值估计和信用分配时，在法律推理、深度搜索和代码定位基准上，FOCUS在每步生成预算相同的条件下优于GRPO和VinePPO；在Qwen3.5-9B规模下，其留出集准确率相比最强基线在BrowseComp-Plus上提高了7.2个百分点（55.4 vs. 48.2），在DeonticBench上提高了4.1个百分点（56.5 vs. 52.4）。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    While diffusion models excel at generating high-quality samples, their latent variables typically lack semantic meaning and are not suitable for representation learning. Here, we propose InfoDiffusion, an algorithm that augments diffusion models with low-dimensional latent variables that capture high-level factors of variation in the data. InfoDiffusion relies on a learning objective regularized with the mutual information between observed and hidden variables, which is designed to improve latent space quality and to prevent the latents from being ignored by expressive diffusion-based decoders. Empirically, we find that InfoDiffusion learns disentangled and human-interpretable latent representations that are competitive with state-of-the-art generative and contrastive methods, while retaining the high sample quality of diffusion models. Our method enables manipulating the attributes of generated images and has the potential to assist tasks that require exploring a learned latent space to generate quality samples, e.g., generative design.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    This survey examines evaluation methods for large language model (LLM)-based agents in multi-turn conversational settings. Using a PRISMA-inspired framework, we systematically reviewed nearly 250 scholarly sources, capturing the state of the art from various venues of publication, and establishing a solid foundation for our analysis. Our study offers a structured approach by developing two interrelated taxonomy systems: one that defines \emph{what to evaluate} and another that explains \emph{how to evaluate}. The first taxonomy identifies key components of LLM-based agents for multi-turn conversations and their evaluation dimensions, including task completion, response quality, user experience, memory and context retention, as well as planning and tool integration. These components ensure that the performance of conversational agents is assessed in a holistic and meaningful manner. The second taxonomy system focuses on the evaluation methodologies. It categorizes approaches into annotation-based evaluations, automated metrics, hybrid strategies that combine human assessments with quantitative measures, and self-judging methods utilizing LLMs. This framework not only captures traditional metrics derived from language understanding, such as BLEU and ROUGE scores, but also incorporates advanced techniques that reflect the dynamic, interactive nature of multi-turn dialogues.

    On the Value of Cross-Modal Misalignment in Multimodal Representation Learning

    多模态表征学习中跨模态错位的价值

    Yichao Cai, Yuhang Liu, Erdun Gao, Tianjiao Jiang, Zhen Zhang, Anton van den Hengel, Javen Qinfeng Shi

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper formalizes two sources of cross-modal misalignment and theoretically characterizes which semantic variables aligned representations recover, supported by empirical studies. This advances understanding of learned representation structure, while composition, reasoning, and systems design are not central.

    本文形式化了跨模态错位的两种来源，并从理论上刻画对齐后的表示能够恢复哪些语义变量，同时提供了实证研究支持。这推进了对学习所得表征结构的理解；组合能力、推理和系统设计并非本文核心。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Multimodal representation learning, exemplified by multimodal contrastive learning (MMCL) using image-text pairs, aims to learn powerful representations by aligning cues across modalities. This approach relies on the core assumption that the exemplar image-text pairs constitute two representations of an identical concept. However, recent research has revealed that real-world datasets often exhibit \emph{cross-modal misalignment}. There are two distinct viewpoints on how to address this issue: one suggests mitigating the misalignment, and the other leveraging it. We seek here to reconcile these seemingly opposing perspectives and to provide a practical guide for practitioners. Using latent variable models, we thus formalize cross-modal misalignment by introducing two specific mechanisms: \emph{selection bias}, where some semantic variables are absent in the text, and \emph{perturbation bias}, where semantic variables are altered---both leading to misalignment in data pairs. Our theoretical analysis shows that, under suitable assumptions, population global minimizers of an alignment--entropy surrogate yield representations that depend only on the semantic variables unaffected by selection and perturbation biases and locally identify this subset almost surely. Extensive empirical studies on synthetic data and real image-text datasets further examine how cross-modal misalignment shapes semantic predictability and downstream performance, shedding light on its nuanced impact on multimodal representation learning.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    A major bottleneck in the training process for Zero-Shot Coordination (ZSC) agents is the generation of diverse partner agents via Population-based Training (PBT). Prominent PBT methods, such as Cross-play Minimization (XPM), can be very computationally expensive and sample inefficient, as the training objective requires sampling multiple types of trajectories, in particular the need of Mixed-Play (MP) trajectories to mitigate self-sabotage in cross-play. Each partner agent in the population is also trained from scratch, despite all of the partners in the population learning policies of the same coordination task. In this work, we propose that simulated trajectories from the dynamics model of an environment can drastically speed up the training process for XPM methods. We introduce XPM-WM, a framework for generating simulated trajectories for XPM via a learned World Model (WM). We show XPM with simulated trajectories removes the need to sample Mixed-Play trajectories while still mitigating any self-sabotage. The learned WM also bootstraps the training of subsequent agents in the population. We show that these two factors combined gives XPM-WM significantly better sample efficiency as compared to other XPM methods and scales linearly to the size of the population. We show our proposed method can effectively generate partners with diverse conventions that match the performance of previous methods. Finally, we show that our proposed training paradigm of using learned world models to generate diverse population can be extended to other PBT methods beyond XPM.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Accurate univariate forecasting remains a pressing need in real-world systems, such as energy markets, hydrology, retail demand, and IoT monitoring, where signals are often intermittent and horizons span both short- and long-term. While transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures are increasingly favored for time-series forecasting, a key gap persists: MoE models typically require complicated training with both the main forecasting loss and auxiliary load-balancing losses, along with careful routing/temperature tuning, which hinders practical adoption. In this paper, we propose a model architecture that simplifies the training process for univariate time series forecasting and effectively addresses both long- and short-term horizons, including intermittent patterns. Our approach combines sparse MoE computation with a novel attention-inspired gating mechanism that replaces the traditional one-layer softmax router. Through extensive empirical evaluation, we demonstrate that our gating design naturally promotes balanced expert utilization and achieves superior predictive accuracy without requiring the auxiliary load-balancing losses typically used in classical MoE implementations. The model achieves better performance while utilizing only a fraction of the parameters required by state-of-the-art transformer models, such as PatchTST. Furthermore, experiments across diverse datasets confirm that our MoE architecture with the proposed gating mechanism is more computationally efficient than LSTM for both long- and short-term forecasting, enabling cost-effective inference. These results highlight the potential of our approach for practical time-series forecasting applications where both accuracy and computational efficiency are critical.

    The goal of agents in multi-agent environments is to maximize total reward against the opposing agents that are encountered. Following a game-theoretic solution concept, such as Nash equilibrium, may obtain a strong performance in some settings; however, such approaches fail to capitalize on historical and observed data from repeated interactions against our opponents. Opponent modeling algorithms integrate machine learning techniques to exploit suboptimal opponents utilizing available data; however, the effectiveness of such approaches in imperfect-information games to date is quite limited. We show that existing opponent modeling approaches fail to satisfy a simple desirable property even against static opponents drawn from a known prior distribution; namely, they do not guarantee that the model approaches the opponent's true strategy even in the limit as the number of iterations approaches infinity.     Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    EVOL-RL addresses diversity collapse in label-free self-improvement with majority-based selection, novelty-based credit, and training regularizers, improving mathematical problem-solving results. It advances reasoning training substantially; response diversity is relevant to variation in composition, but the abstract does not study compositional generalization.

    EVOL-RL 通过基于多数意见的选择、基于新颖性的信用分配和训练正则化来应对无标签自我改进中的多样性坍塌，并提升数学问题求解结果。它显著推进了推理训练；回复多样性与组合变化有关，但摘要没有研究组合泛化。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large language models (LLMs) can improve through reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), but many settings lack reference answers or external verifiers. Label-free self-improvement instead constructs training signals from the model's own outputs. Because the same policy generates both the candidate responses and the signals derived from them, each update also changes the candidates available for future training, creating a self-reinforcing feedback loop. We identify a failure mode of this loop, which we call selection-induced diversity collapse: repeated self-selection can progressively narrow the candidate pool and make alternative correct solutions harder to sample. To address this problem, we propose EVOL-RL, which balances selection and variation. Majority voting provides a stable selection signal, while embedding-based novelty refines credit among responses with the same selection status; entropy regularization and asymmetric clipping further support this process by maintaining diverse rollouts and preserving rare, high-advantage updates. Across multiple training distributions, model scales, backbones, and matched label-free baselines, EVOL-RL consistently improves pass@n while generally maintaining or improving pass@1. For example, when trained without labels on AIME24, Qwen3-4B-Base improves over TTRL on held-out AIME25 from 4.6% to 17.1% in pass@1 and from 18.5% to 42.0% in pass@16. Training analyses further show that when the current majority is wrong, EVOL-RL better preserves alternative correct solutions. The code is available at: https://github.com/YujunZhou/EVOL-RL.

    Post-training LLM compression often relies on low-rank approximations, which force all columns of a projection matrix to share a single low-dimensional subspace. We propose CoSpaDi, a training-free compression framework that replaces this single-subspace assumption with a union-of-subspaces model via sparse dictionary learning. CoSpaDi factorizes each weight matrix into a dense dictionary and column-sparse coefficients, allowing different columns to select different subsets of dictionary atoms at the same storage budget. To preserve model behavior, we use calibration activations to transform functional reconstruction into a standard dictionary learning problem. Across LLaMA and Qwen models, CoSpaDi improves accuracy-compression and perplexity-compression trade-offs over SVD-based and structured pruning baselines at 20-40\% compression ratios, while naturally supporting sparse-dense computation and post-training quantization of sparse coefficients.

ROSA guides the model parameters toward a theoretical optimal policy in a single, efficient update step, avoiding costly iterative gradient-based optimization and minimizing computational overhead.     Large language models (LLMs) still struggle with multi-hop reasoning over knowledge-graphs (KGs), and we identify a previously overlooked structural reason for this difficulty: Transformer attention heads naturally specialize in distinct semantic relations across reasoning stages, forming a hop-aligned relay pattern. This key finding suggests that multi-hop reasoning is inherently multi-view, yet existing KG-based retrieval-augmented generation (KG-RAG) systems collapse all reasoning hops into a single representation, flat embedding space, suppressing this implicit structure and causing noisy or drifted path exploration. We introduce ParallaxRAG, a symmetric multi-view framework that decouples queries and KGs into aligned, head-specific semantic spaces. By enforcing relational diversity across multiple heads while constraining weakly related paths, ParallaxRAG constructs more accurate, cleaner subgraphs and guides LLMs through grounded, hop-wise reasoning. On WebQSP and CWQ, it achieves state-of-the-art retrieval and QA performance, substantially reduces hallucination, and generalizes strongly to the biomedical BioASQ benchmark.

    大型语言模型（LLM）在知识图谱（KG）上的多跳推理方面仍面临困难。我们发现了一个此前被忽视的结构性原因：Transformer 注意力头会自然地专门处理推理不同阶段的不同语义关系，从而形成与跳数对齐的接力模式。这一关键发现表明，多跳推理本质上具有多视图特性；然而，现有基于 KG 的检索增强生成（KG-RAG）系统将所有推理跳数压缩到单一表示和扁平嵌入空间中，抑制了这种隐式结构，导致路径探索出现噪声或偏移。我们提出 ParallaxRAG，这是一种对称的多视图框架，将查询和 KG 解耦到对齐的、针对不同注意力头的语义空间中。通过在多个注意力头之间强化关系多样性，同时约束关联较弱的路径，ParallaxRAG 构建出更准确、更清晰的子图，并引导 LLM 进行有依据的逐跳推理。在 WebQSP 和 CWQ 上，它取得了最先进的检索和问答性能，大幅减少幻觉，并能很好地泛化到生物医学基准 BioASQ。

    ENGLISH

    Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has delivered impressive gains in mathematical and multimodal reasoning and has become a standard post-training paradigm for contemporary language and vision-language models. However, the RLVR recipe introduces a significant risk of capability regression, in which models forget foundational skills after prolonged training without employing regularization strategies. We empirically confirm this concern, observing that open-source reasoning models suffer performance degradation on core capabilities such as perception and faithfulness. While imposing regularization terms like KL divergence can help prevent deviation from the base model, these terms are computed on the current task and therefore do not guarantee preservation of broader knowledge. Meanwhile, commonly used experience replay across heterogeneous domains makes it nontrivial to decide how much training emphasis each objective should receive. To address this, we propose RECAP-a replay strategy with dynamic objective reweighting for general knowledge preservation. Our reweighting mechanism adapts online using short-horizon signals of convergence and instability, shifting the post-training focus away from saturated objectives and toward underperforming or volatile ones. Our method is end-to-end and readily applicable to existing RLVR pipelines without training additional models or heavy tuning. Extensive experiments on benchmarks using Qwen2.5-VL-3B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, which not only preserves general capabilities but also improves reasoning by enabling more flexible trade-offs among in-task rewards.

    Understanding and replicating human mobility requires not only spatial-temporal accuracy but also an awareness of the cognitive hierarchy underlying real-world travel decisions. Traditional agent-based or deep learning models can reproduce statistical patterns of movement but fail to capture the semantic coherence and causal logic of human behavior. Large language models (LLMs) show potential, but struggle to balance creative reasoning with strict structural compliance. This study proposes a Hierarchical LLM-Agent Framework, termed Narrative-to-Action, that integrates high-level narrative reasoning, mid-level reflective planning, and low-level behavioral execution within a unified cognitive hierarchy. At the macro level, one agent is employed as a "creative writer" to produce diary-style narratives rich in motivation and context, then uses another agent as a "structural parser" to convert narratives into machine-readable plans. At the micro level, the agent executes concrete actions-selecting locations, transportation modes, and time intervals-through interaction with an environmental simulation. By embedding this multi-layer cognitive process, the framework produces not only synthetic trajectories that align closely with real-world patterns but also interpretable representations of human decision logic. This research advances synthetic mobility generation from a data-driven paradigm to a cognition-driven simulation, providing a scalable pathway for understanding, predicting, and synthesizing complex urban mobility behaviors through hierarchical LLM agents.

Instructional Memory retains identified global constraints in a dedicated prefix.     Generating humorous memes is a challenging multimodal task that moves beyond direct image-to-caption supervision. It requires a nuanced reasoning over visual content, contextual cues, and subjective humor. First, HUMOR employs a hierarchical, multi-path Chain-of-Thought (CoT): the model begins by identifying a template-level intent, then explores diverse reasoning paths under different contexts, and finally anchors onto a high-quality, context-specific path. This CoT supervision, which traces back from ground-truth captions, enhances reasoning diversity. We further analyze that this multi-path exploration with anchoring maintains a high expected humor quality, under the practical condition that high-quality paths retain significant probability mass. Second, to capture subjective humor, we train a pairwise reward model that operates within groups of memes sharing the same template. Following established theory, this approach ensures a consistent and robust proxy for human preference, even with subjective and noisy labels. The reward model then enables a group-wise reinforcement learning optimization, guaranteeing providing a theoretical guarantee for monotonic improvement within the trust region. Extensive experiments show that HUMOR empowers various VLMs with superior reasoning diversity, more reliable preference alignment, and higher overall meme quality. Beyond memes, our work presents a general training paradigm for open-ended, human-aligned multimodal generation, where success is guided by comparative judgment within coherent output group.

Yet, their adversarial robustness remains critically unexplored. This paper studies the phenomenon whereby specific short input phrases induce a partial amnesia effect in such models, by irreversibly overwriting information in their hidden states, referred to as a Hidden State Poisoning Attack (HiSPA). Our benchmark RoBench-25 allows evaluating a model's information retrieval capabilities when subject to HiSPAs, and confirms the vulnerability of SSMs against such attacks. Even the recent Jamba-1.7-Mini SSM--Transformer (a 52B hybrid model) collapses on RoBench-25 under some HiSPA triggers, whereas pure Transformers do not. Finally, our interpretability study reveals patterns in Mamba's hidden layers during HiSPAs that could be used to build a HiSPA mitigation system.     We study tabular finite-horizon reinforcement learning problems with multiple steps of lookahead information. Before acting, the learner observes $\ell$ steps of future transition and reward realizations: the exact state the agent would reach and the rewards it would collect under any possible course of action. While it has been shown that such information can drastically boost the value, finding the optimal policy is NP-hard, and it is common to apply one of two tractable heuristics: processing the lookahead in chunks of predefined sizes ('fixed batching policies'), and model predictive control. We first illustrate the problems with these two approaches and propose utilizing the lookahead in adaptive (state-dependent) batches; we refer to such policies as adaptive batching policies (ABPs). We derive the optimal Bellman equations for these strategies and design an optimistic regret-minimizing algorithm that enables learning the optimal ABP when interacting with unknown environments. Our regret bounds are order-optimal up to a potential factor of the lookahead horizon $\ell$, which can usually be considered a small constant.

    ENGLISH

    Large language models (LLMs) increasingly rely on external knowledge to improve factuality, yet many knowledge sources on the Web, such as scholarly indexes and product catalogs, are organized as heterogeneous graphs. Reasoning over such graph-structured knowledge poses two key challenges: (1) navigating structured, schema-defined relations requires precise function calls beyond similarity-based retrieval, and (2) answering complex questions often demands multi-hop evidence aggregation through iterative information seeking. We study how LLMs can learn these interaction capabilities and transfer them to unseen domains. We propose GraphDancer, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that teaches LLMs to navigate graphs by interleaving reasoning and function execution. To improve RL for moderate-sized LLMs, we introduce a graph-aware curriculum that schedules training by the structural difficulty of questions using an easy-to-hard biased sampler. We evaluate GraphDancer on the multi-domain GRBench benchmark, training only on Academic and Biomedical graphs. Testing covers held-out questions from these domains as well as unseen E-commerce, Literature, and Legal graphs. With either Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct or Qwen3-14B as the backbone, GraphDancer outperforms graph-agent baselines using the same backbone across all evaluation domains. These results indicate that the learned graph exploration and reasoning capabilities transfer across domains. On average across unseen domains, GraphDancer with a 14B backbone also outperforms baselines powered by the closed-source models GPT-4.1-mini and GPT-5-nano. Trajectory analyses further show that GraphDancer retrieves answer-bearing evidence more often and achieves higher accuracy when such evidence is found, while substantially reducing invalid-protocol outcomes.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    本文将 EEG 分类器特征与基于生物物理学的脑回路模拟联系起来，利用 1/f 斜率和连接性解释与疾病相关的频谱变化。这为理解脑回路机制提供了深入见解，但并未研究 AI 模型内部的机制或表征；SNN 分类器是其应用背景。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    As the prevalence of Alzheimer's disease (AD) rises, improving mechanistic insight from non-invasive biomarkers is increasingly critical. Recent work suggests that circuit-level brain alterations manifest as changes in electroencephalography (EEG) spectral features detectable by machine learning. However, conventional deep learning approaches for EEG-based AD detection are computationally intensive and mechanistically opaque. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer a biologically plausible and energy-efficient alternative, yet their application to AD diagnosis remains largely unexplored. We propose a neuro-bridge framework that links data-driven learning with minimal, biophysically grounded simulations, enabling bidirectional interpretation between machine learning signatures and circuit-level mechanisms in AD. Using resting-state clinical EEG, we train an SNN classifier that achieves competitive performance (AUC = 0.839) and identifies the aperiodic 1/f slope as a key discriminative marker. The 1/f slope reflects excitation-inhibition balance. To interpret this mechanistically, we construct spiking network simulations in which inhibitory-to-excitatory synaptic ratios are systematically varied to emulate healthy, mild cognitive impairment, and AD-like states. Using both membrane potential-based and synaptic current-based EEG proxies, we reproduce empirical spectral slowing and altered alpha organization. Incorporating empirical functional connectivity priors into multi-subnetwork simulations further enhances spectral differentiation, demonstrating that large-scale network topology constrains EEG signatures more strongly than excitation-inhibition balance alone. Overall, this neuro-bridge approach connects SNN-based classification with interpretable circuit simulations, advancing mechanistic understanding of EEG biomarkers while enabling scalable, explainable AD detection.

    Generative AI (GenAI) has transformed applications in natural language processing and content creation, yet centralized inference remains hindered by high latency, limited customizability, and privacy concerns. Deploying large models (LMs) in mobile edge networks emerges as a promising solution. However, it also poses new challenges, including heterogeneous multi-modal LMs with diverse resource demands and inference speeds, varied prompt/output modalities that complicate orchestration, and resource-limited infrastructure ill-suited for concurrent LM execution. In response, we propose a Multi-Agentic AI framework for latency- and fairness-aware multi-modal LM inference in mobile edge networks. Experiments demonstrate that our solution reduces average end-to-end latency by 42.9% compared with a state-of-the-art online-learning baseline and by 80.6% compared with the full-activation baseline, while maintaining a mean service-type Jain's index of 0.925. To address this issue, we propose SAYO, a visual reasoning model trained with a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that introduces a region-level visual attention-based reward. This reward explicitly aligns optimization signals with visually grounded reasoning steps, enabling the model to learn more reliable attention behaviors. Extensive experiments across multiple multimodal benchmarks demonstrate that SAYO consistently improves performance on diverse reasoning and perception tasks.
